newsitem.title: USA: Florida citrus belt sees cooler temperatures.
newsitem.headline: Florida citrus belt sees cooler temperatures.

text.p: Isolated low lying areas of the Florida citrus belt saw some light scattered frost during the week ended Dec 15, with last Monday bringing in the coldest temperatures of the season, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said.
Temperatures fell to the mid to upper thirties, FASS said, with cool weather holding new growth in check.

FASS said many caretakers were running their irrigation systems, as dry conditions prevailed all week. Caretakers are also cutting cover crops prior to harvesting and for fire protection. Growers are placing and fueling heaters in isolated areas.
Most early fruit is in very good condition and the harvest of early and midseason oranges active in all areas.
Movement of Navels for promotionals, gift fruit and general fresh packing and shipping is at the busiest time of the year, FASS said.
They reported an estimated 699,000 boxes of Navel oranges were harvested in the week ended December 15, up from 691,000 boxes in the previous week and 312,000 boxes in the week ended December 1.
An estimated 8,347,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended December 15, up from 8,364,000 boxes the prior week and 4,871,000 boxes the week ended December 1, FASS said.
